case_name: Tushar Hasmukhbhai Shah v Manilal Pitambardas and Others
facts: The eight workmen were retrenched by M/s. Gujarat Pharmaceutical and Chemical Works.
It was a case of closure of the independent unit, namely, Chemical Section of the Factory;
The dispute before the Labour Court could not be adjudicated before the Labour Court and it could have been referred to the Industrial Tribunal.
It is the admitted position that the entire factory was closed in 1985, there was no ground to order for payment of the backwages thereafter.
None of these contentions were acceptable to the High Court for the reasons recorded in the impugned judgment.
The writ petition was dismissed affirming the Award passed by the Labour Court.

In the argument, the learned counsel submitted that it was not a case of retrenchment and in fact the factory had paid a closure compensation and once the respondent-workmen had accepted that compensation, it was not open to them to challenge their retrenchment.

The second contention as to the jurisdiction of the Labour Court, we may only state that the High Court has rightly noticed that it was permissible under the Proviso to S. 10(1) of the Industrial Disputes Act that a dispute could be decided by the Labour Court.
Thus, viewing from any angle, we do not find any good ground or valid reason to upset the concurrent findings of fact recorded by the Labour Court as well as the High Court.
The appeal is dismissed. No costs.
The learned counsel contended that the High Court committed an error in directing the arrest of the petitioner without there being any proper order;
No contempt proceedings can be initiated for breach or disobedience of the Award of the Labour Court.
issues: It was not a case of retrenchment but it was a case of closure of the independent unit, namely, Chemical Section of the Factory;
The dispute before the Labour Court could not be adjudicated before the Labour Court and it could have been referred to the Industrial Tribunal.
It is the admitted position that the entire factory was closed in 1985, there was no ground to order for payment of the backwages thereafter.
Whether the Labour Court had jurisdiction to decide the case
Whether the High Court committed an error in directing the arrest of the petitioner without there being any proper order
petitioner_arguments: It was not a case of retrenchment and in fact the factory had paid a closure compensation and once the respondent-workmen had accepted that compensation, it was not open to them to challenge their retrenchment.
The Labour Court as well as the High Court committed serious error in not accepting the case of the appellant; it was a case of closure and not retrenchment.
No contempt proceedings can be initiated for breach or disobedience of the Award of the Labour Court.
respondent_arguments: It is the admitted position that the entire factory was closed in 1985, there was no ground to order for payment of the backwages thereafter.
The dispute before the Labour Court could not be adjudicated before the Labour Court and it could have been referred to the Industrial Tribunal.
The Award passed by the Labour Court was challenged before the High Court invoking jurisdiction u/art. 227 of the Constitution of India.
court_reasoning: We do not find any good ground or valid reason to upset the concurrent findings of fact recorded by the Labour Court as well as the High Court.
It is not a case where we should exercise our jurisdiction u/art. 136 of the Constitution of India having due regard to the facts and circumstances of the case.
The appeal is dismissed. No costs.
We do not express one way or the other as to the maintainability of the contempt proceedings as they are pending before the High Court.
holding: The appeal is dismissed. No costs.
This petition does not survive. The special leave petition is disposed of accordingly.
